title: the artifact journal seals segments at a fixed entry count and verify_chain replays them whole
intention: A root's artifact journal stays under GitHub's per-file limits as it grows: past a fixed entry count the head seals into an ordered segment, and read_journal and verify_chain replay segments then head as one unbroken chain from genesis.
why: Measured 2026-11-15: the Dell push of cairn/.artifact-journal.jsonl was 50.04 MB and GitHub warned GH001 (the hard refusal is at 100 MB); on akiendelllinux the same file is 33 MB over 22895 entries. The journal is the who/when record of every record write, and one growing file is a push GitHub will refuse. The orchestrator grepped the corpus and found no ticket on journal size or rotation.
traces_to: Law 7: errors are permanent in records of truth, and a record of truth that cannot be pushed is lost off the box. Law 4: the bound is enforced by the appending door, not by remembering to trim.
how: The head keeps its path, .artifact-journal.jsonl, so every appender and path reader keeps working. When an append makes entry N*K (counted from genesis, so every box cuts at the same entry), artifact moves the head's entries into .artifact-journal/<NNNN>.jsonl (zero-padded, ordered by name) and starts a new head whose first entry's prev is the sealed segment's last entry sha. read_journal and verify_chain read the sealed segments in name order, then the head. K is a module constant chosen to keep a segment well under 50 MB (about 1.4 KB per entry measured, so K = 20000 gives about 28 MB). The build censuses the six path readers and routes any whole-file replay through read_journal. A red-first proof builds a scratch root with K overridden small.

clauses.claim: a scratch root whose journal passes the bound K is split on append into a sealed .artifact-journal/0001.jsonl and a head, each holding at most K entries, and verify_chain over the root returns no faults
a one-byte edit in the sealed segment makes verify_chain name a fault, and so does a head whose first prev does not equal the sealed segment's last entry sha
read_journal returns every entry in order across the sealed segments and the head, equal to the entries appended
two roots that append the same entries cut at the same entry and seal byte-identical segments

decisions.text: D1: the appender in artifact.py seals the head into .artifact-journal/<NNNN>.jsonl when an append makes entry N*K from genesis; read_journal and verify_chain read the segments in name order, then the head.

D2: census the readers that name .artifact-journal by path (build_inspector/inspector.py, tester red_tickets.py and hollow.py, cc scripts prove.sh and close.sh, the installer). A reader that replays the whole file is routed through read_journal. A reader of the head only is left alone and named in the proof's why. A reader outside artifact that must change is a ticket of its own (RULE 1), cast from the census.
D3: the red-first proof builds a scratch root with K overridden small, one tooth per clause.

out: every other component; a path reader that must change is its own ticket
